title: The Order-K Boole Summation Limit: Alternating-Series Remainder via Higher Forward Differences

problemStatement.formal: For a null sequence $a\to 0$ with convergent alternating series $\lim_{m\to\infty}\operatorname{altSum}(a,n,m)=S$, pass the finite order-$K$ Boole identity to the limit: $S=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\frac{(-1)^{k}}{2^{k+1}}(-1)^{n}(\Delta^{k}a)_{n}-\frac{(-1)^{K-1}}{2^{K}}T_{K}$, where $\Delta^{k}a$ is the $k$-th forward difference, $\operatorname{altSum}(b,n,m)=\sum_{j=n}^{m-1}(-1)^{j}b_j$, and $T_{K}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\operatorname{altSum}(\Delta^{K}a,n,m)$.
problemStatement.plain: The parent entry passed Boole's summation identity to the limit at first order, tying the sum S of a convergent alternating series to the limit of its first forward-difference series. This problem does the same at every order K at once: carry the finite general-order identity boole_general to the limit m to infinity, expressing S through the limits of the higher forward-difference series and the Euler/Boole weights (-1)^k/2^{k+1}. The only analytic input is that each signed endpoint term vanishes for a null sequence; the new work is an induction on K and finite-sum bookkeeping.
whyMatters: Boole summation is the alternating-series analogue of Euler-Maclaurin, whose practical remainder/acceleration payoff only appears at general order K; the parent's first-order result is just the base case.
It turns the finite order-K Boole engine into a genuine convergence and remainder tool inside Mathlib, expressing the value of a convergent alternating series through higher forward differences.
It supplies a reusable template for passing an exact finite summation identity, parameterized by an order K, to a Filter.Tendsto limit statement.

open: The general-order limit statement: passing boole_general (order K) to the limit m to infinity to obtain the closed identity for arbitrary K.
Convergence of every intermediate higher forward-difference series altSum(Delta^k a, n, .) for 0 <= k <= K, so the boundary sum is well defined in the limit.
An unconditional (antitone null) version at general order via the alternating-series test, and identification of the remainder with Mathlib's two-sided alternating-series tail bounds.
knownResults.goal: Prove the order-K limit form of Boole's identity for a convergent alternating series of a null sequence: pass boole_general to m to infinity, establish existence of the K-th forward-difference series limit T_K, and derive the closed identity relating S, the boundary terms (Delta^k a)_n, and T_K with weights (-1)^k/2^{k+1}, plus an unconditional corollary for antitone null sequences.
